note: Casual; use 저 in polite speech. 나 + 가 → 내가.

ex.en: I'm hungry too.
I'll have coffee.
Want to watch a movie with me this weekend?

note: Pattern -지 않다; in speech 안 + verb is more common.

ex.en: It's not very cold today.
This food isn't spicy.
Minho doesn't drink alcohol.

note: Also "he" in writing; in speech say 그 사람.

ex.en: That movie was really fun.
Where is that store?
What's that person's name?

note: Sino-Korean numbers: 일 년, 이 년. 작년 = last year.

ex.en: It's been two years since I came to Korea.
I worked at this company for five years.
I travel once a year.

note: Also "my" for family/home: 우리 엄마, 우리 집.

ex.en: Let's have lunch together tomorrow.
My house is near the school.
Our team won!

note: Verb + -(으)ㄹ 때 = when ~.

ex.en: I lived in Busan when I was little.

ex.s: 밥 먹을 때 휴대폰 보지 마세요.
ex.en: Don't look at your phone while you eat.
When I'm tired, I go to bed early.

note: N + 중이다 = in the middle of N: 회의 중.

ex.en: I'm in a meeting right now.

ex.s: 이 두 개 중에서 뭐가 좋아요?
ex.en: Which of these two is better?
I'm driving now, so I'll call you later.

note: 전화를 받다 = to answer the phone.

ex.en: Did you get a birthday present?
Do you take cards here?
Why didn't you answer the phone?

note: Only for close friends or younger people. 너 + 가 → 네가 (said 니가).

ex.en: Do you want to come too?
What are you doing today?
You're a really good cook!

note: ㄹ-irregular: 만들어요, 만드세요, 만든.

ex.en: I made gimbap.
My dad made this chair.
Making friends isn't easy.

note: 말하다 = to speak. Homonym: 말 = horse.

ex.en: Please speak slowly.
Is what you said true?
You speak Korean well.

en: to be visible; to look, seem
note: -아/어 보이다 = to look ~: 피곤해 보여요.

ex.en: You can see the ocean from here.
The letters are small, so I can't see well.
You look tired today.

note: N + 때문에; verb + -기 때문에.

ex.en: Traffic is bad because of the rain.
I couldn't go to school because of a cold.
I didn't buy it because it was too expensive.

note: 여자 친구 = girlfriend. Polite: 여자분.

ex.en: That woman is the teacher.
Where's the women's restroom?
Do you have a girlfriend, Minho?

en: to be unable to; to be bad at
note: One word when meaning "bad at": 노래를 못해요.

ex.en: I can't swim.
I couldn't work out today.
I'm not good at cooking.

note: Short form 갖다. 가지고 가다 = to take along.

ex.en: Do you have a pen?
Can I have this?
Take an umbrella with you.

note: Joins sentences; between nouns use 하고 or 와/과.

ex.en: I ate. And then I took a walk.
Coffee, please. And some water too.
Did you do your homework? And clean your room?
Call me when you come out of the subway station.
When will the food come out?
This song was in a drama.

note: Same as 같이, slightly more formal.

ex.en: I had dinner with my family.
Let's take a picture together!
I went on a trip with a friend.

note: 남자 친구 = boyfriend. Polite: 남자분.

ex.en: Who is that man?
The men's restroom is on the second floor.
Ji-woo's boyfriend is a chef.

note: A sports match is 경기.

ex.en: I played video games at home on the weekend.
What games do you like?
My kid plays video games too much.
I really like this kind of weather.
Do you have this style in other colors?
Nothing like this has happened to me before.

note: N 위에 = on/above N. Opposite: 아래, 밑.

ex.en: The keys are on the desk.
Who lives upstairs?
Please put it on top of the fridge.

note: A bit formal; in speech -고 싶다 is more common.

ex.en: Choose the color you want.
If you want, let's go together.
I bought the present my child wanted.
Everyone laughed.
Everything on the menu is delicious.
Every room has air conditioning.

en: to look for, find; to withdraw (money)

ex.en: Did you find my phone?
I'm looking for the restroom.
I'll withdraw some money at the bank.
If there's a problem, get in touch.
Something's wrong with my car.
The test questions were too hard.
Let's talk somewhere quiet.
This is my favorite place.
There's no place to park.

note: N 안에. Different from the adverb 안 "not".

ex.en: What's in the bag?
I'll wait inside the building.
I'll arrive within an hour.

note: In casual speech 근데 is more common.

ex.en: It's expensive. But it's really good.
I want to go. But I don't have time.
I'm tired, but I'm happy.
What time does the movie start?
I'm starting yoga next week.
Let's start the meeting.

note: Same as 제일; 가장 is slightly more formal.

ex.en: Where's the nearest pharmacy?

ex.s: 여기서 가장 인기 있는 메뉴가 뭐예요?
ex.en: What's the most popular dish here?
Family is the most important thing.
I'm going to sleep as soon as I get home.
The pharmacy is right next to the bank.
That's exactly what I mean.
Don't say things like that.
That's happened to me too.
Do you like that kind of movie?

note: N 앞에 = in front of N. Opposite: 뒤.

ex.en: Let's meet in front of the school.
Go straight ahead.
I sat in the front seat of the bus.

note: -아/어 죽겠다 = "so ~ I could die": 배고파 죽겠어요.

ex.en: I'm starving.
My pet fish died.
The flowers died because I didn't water them.

note: As "yeah" only with close friends; polite is 네.

ex.en: Oh, it's raining!
Oh, is it already ten?

ex.s: 어, 민호 씨! 여기서 뭐 해요?
ex.en: Oh, Minho! What are you doing here?

note: In casual speech 쓰다 is more common.

ex.en: Can I use this computer?
You can only use cash.
This app is easy to use.
It takes about 30 minutes.
I have about 10,000 won.
I study about two hours a day.

note: ㄷ-irregular: 들어요, 들었어요, 듣는.

ex.en: I like listening to music.
Did you hear about that?
I didn't catch that. Please say it again.
What did you do during vacation?
I waited for three hours.

ex.s: 제가 없는 동안 강아지 좀 봐 주세요.
ex.en: Please watch my dog while I'm away.

note: 마음에 들다 = to like (something).

ex.en: I like these clothes.
I've been feeling at ease lately.
Let me know if you change your mind.

note: Only before nouns: 첫날, 첫 번째.

ex.en: Today is my first day at the company.
How was your first date?
I bought my parents a gift with my first paycheck.
I have to go now.
It doesn't hurt anymore.
I can eat Korean food well now.

note: 사랑하다 = to love.

ex.en: I love you, Mom.
Do you remember your first love?
Our puppy gets a lot of love.

note: After -아/어 it means "completely": 잊어버리다.

ex.en: Please take out the trash.
I'll have to throw this milk out.
I threw out all my old clothes.

en: what kind of; which; a certain

ex.en: What kind of food do you like?
Which one is better?
Someone came looking for you.
The kids go to school at 8.
What are you doing after school?
I'm a teacher at this school.
I don't have much money.
I spent a lot of money this month.
Can you lend me some money?

note: ㄹ-irregular: 들어요, 드는. 마음에 들다 = to like.

ex.en: I'll carry your bag for you.
Don't lift heavy things.
Getting ready for a wedding costs a lot of money.
Why were you late?
I'm in a good mood for no reason.
Is there a reason you're learning Korean?

note: Also a noun: 모두가 = everyone.

ex.en: How much is it altogether?
Everyone in my family is healthy.
Is everyone here?
Wash your hands before eating.
My hands are so cold.
Raise your hand if you have a question.
There's a lot of food left over.
How much time is left?
I bought coffee with the leftover money.
Which team do you root for?
There are five people on our team.
The team dinner is on Friday.

note: 속이 안 좋다 = to have an upset stomach.

ex.en: My stomach is upset.
The key is in my pocket.
I saw my grandma in my dream.

note: Spoken short forms: 놔요, 놨어요.

ex.en: I'll put the keys here.
Put your bag on the chair.
I don't know where I put my phone.

note: Homonym: 밤 = chestnut.

ex.en: I couldn't sleep last night.
Don't walk around alone at night.
Sorry for calling so late at night.
I finished all my homework.
Did you eat it all?
Everyone in my family is tall.

note: 날씨 = weather; 생일날 = birthday.

ex.en: It's a nice day today.
What did you do on your birthday?
I'm leaving the next morning.

note: 줄(을) 서다 = to stand in line.

ex.en: Do I need to line up here?
The line is too long.
My earphone cord got tangled.

note: 약속을 잡다 = to make plans.

ex.en: I'll catch a taxi.
Hold on tight to the handle.
Let's make plans for next week.

note: 최고예요! = It's the best!

ex.en: This place's tteokbokki is the best.
Today's weather is perfect.
My mom is the best.

en: to pay; to hand in; to make (time)
note: 제가 낼게요 = It's on me.

ex.en: It's on me today.
When do I have to hand in the homework?

ex.s: 시간 좀 내 줄 수 있어요?
ex.en: Can you spare some time for me?
Do you have a good way to do it?
Do you know how to use this?
There's no other way.
What's that sound?
Please turn the volume down.

ex.s: 옆집 개 짖는 소리 때문에 못 잤어요.
ex.en: I couldn't sleep because the neighbor's dog was barking.

note: Short for 아이. 애들 = kids.

ex.en: The kids are already asleep.
How old is your kid?
That kid is in my class.

note: N 뒤에 = behind N; -(으)ㄴ 뒤에 = after ~ing.

ex.en: There's a park behind my house.
Can I sit in the back?
Take the medicine after you eat.
This is an important document.
Health is the most important thing.
I have an important exam tomorrow.

note: Short for 그런데; very common in speech.

ex.en: By the way, what time is it?
It's tasty. But it's a bit salty.
But why didn't you call?

note: 잘 들어가세요 = "Get home safely."

ex.en: Please go inside.
Did you get home okay?
Can I go into the meeting room?

note: What is needed takes 이/가: 돈이 필요해요.

ex.en: Do you need help?
Do you need a bag?
You need a passport when you travel.

note: Spoken short form 얘기. 이야기하다 = to talk.

ex.en: Let's talk later.
Tell me an interesting story.
Grandma told us an old story.

note: 르-irregular: 불러요, 불렀어요.

ex.en: Come in when your name is called.
Should I call you a taxi?
I like singing.
What country are you from?
I like food from other countries too.
Is there a country you'd like to visit?
I've been feeling a lot of stress lately.
Did you feel the earthquake yesterday?
I felt a lot of things while traveling.

note: Often used as "actually": 사실은…

ex.en: Actually, today is my birthday.
Is that true?
Actually, I haven't done my homework yet.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 새로운, 새로워요. Before nouns, 새 is also common.

ex.en: I made a new friend.
There's a new item on the menu.
Everything about this job is new to me.

note: ㄹ-irregular: 힘들어요, 힘든.

ex.en: Work was really hard today.
It's hard to climb the stairs.
If you're tired, take a break.
Which city do you live in?
Seoul is a big city.
This city is really pretty at night.

note: 끝나다 = to end; 끝내다 = to finish.

ex.en: There's a café at the end of this street.
The end of the movie was a little sad.
Don't give up until the end.
Coffee without sugar, please.
I went out without an umbrella.
Can I go in without a reservation?
It's between the bank and the post office.
What's the relationship between you two?
We're close friends.

note: Homonym: 경기 = economy. A video game is 게임.

ex.en: Did you watch the soccer game yesterday?
What time does the match start?
My son is playing in a basketball game today.
Is this the last bus?
Let me ask just one last thing.
Today is the last day of class.
I read before bed.
Did you read my message?
Could you read me the menu?

note: 계획하다 = to plan. 계획을 세우다 = to make a plan.

ex.en: Do you have plans this weekend?
I made travel plans.
What are your plans for this year?

note: 두고 오다 = to leave something behind.

ex.en: I left my wallet at home.
Can I leave my bag here?
Where did you put the car keys?

note: 여러 가지 = various kinds.

ex.en: I've traveled to many countries.
I called several times.

ex.s: 이 빵집에는 여러 가지 빵이 있어요.
ex.en: This bakery has all kinds of bread.

note: Native numbers: 한 달, 두 달.

ex.s: 한 달에 한 번 머리를 잘라요.
ex.en: I get a haircut once a month.
I'm moving next month.
The moon is really bright tonight.

note: 새해 = New Year. 올해 = this year.

ex.en: The sun is so hot.
It gets cold when the sun goes down.
Happy New Year!

note: Also 대학교. 대학생 = college student.

ex.en: Which college did you go to?
My daughter started college this year.
I met up with a friend from college.

note: In speech 벌써 is also very common.

ex.en: I already ate.
The tickets are already sold out.
I've already seen that movie.
A week has already gone by.
Does this bus go past City Hall?
This milk is past its expiration date.

note: 노래하다 = to sing. 노래방 = karaoke.

ex.en: What's the name of this song?
Do you want to go to karaoke?
My kid sings well.
Your room is really clean.
Do you have a room for tonight?
Did you clean your room?

note: 하루 종일 = all day.

ex.en: It rained all day.
How was your day?
How many glasses of water do you drink a day?

note: 가능하면 = if possible.

ex.en: Can I pay by card?
Is delivery possible tomorrow?
Please come early if you can.
Please give me some travel information.
There's a lot of information online.
Don't give out personal information over the phone.

note: 세상에! = "Oh my gosh!"

ex.en: Oh my gosh, really?
It's a small world!
This is the most delicious thing in the world.
